title: Task queue with RabbitMQ
scenario: Lab report PDFs are generated in the request thread; at peak, reports are lost when a server restarts.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · RabbitMQ 4.1 · Spring AMQP 4.1 (@RabbitListener, publisher confirms, retry, dead-letter exchange) · Testcontainers · Awaitility

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Reports in the request

    At Mediqo, the doctor's "get report" click made the PDF in the request itself. At peak, requests waited; a server restart in the middle lost the reports being made.

  2. A queue that forgets

    A queue fixed the waiting. But the workers used auto-ack: RabbitMQ treated a report as done the moment it handed it to a worker. A worker that restarted mid-report took that report with it.

  3. The fix

    The broker confirms each message before the API says "accepted". A worker acknowledges only after the PDF is saved; if it dies, the broker gives the report to another worker. Reports that fail three times wait in a dead-letter queue with the reason.

A message is safe only until someone says it is done. Say it after the work, never before.

What are we building?

A render queue for lab reports: the API puts a request on a durable queue, workers turn it into a PDF, and nothing is lost when a worker dies.

An everyday analogy

A courier signs for a parcel only when it is in the customer's hands. If the courier's van breaks down, the depot still has the parcel on its books and sends another courier. Parcels that cannot be delivered after three tries go to the returns office with a note.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Send: the API publishes the request and waits for the broker's confirmation, then answers 202.
  2. Take: a worker takes one message at a time (prefetch 1).
  3. Finish: the worker saves the PDF; only then is the message acknowledged and deleted.
  4. Give up well: after three failed tries, the message goes to the dead-letter queue and the report shows why.
Check yourself: the worker saves the PDF, then dies before acknowledging. What happens?

The broker gives the message to another worker, marked as redelivered. That worker finds the PDF already there and skips it. Delivery is at least once, so workers must be safe to repeat.

What this station is not

  • No real lab system. Rendering is simulated; the PDFs are minimal.
  • One machine's disk. Reports would go to object storage with several servers.
  • No sign-in. Access control is another station's topic.

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Mediqo (a fictional diagnostics lab): lab report PDFs are generated in the request thread; at peak, reports are lost when a server restarts.

Acceptance criteria

Demo rules: reports LR-0001 to LR-0500; 3 tries, 1 s then 2 s apart; one report per worker at a time; two workers.

  1. Given a known report, then 202 only after the broker has confirmed the message, and later READY with a PDF.
  2. Given the broker unreachable or refusing the message, then 503, and asking again tries again.
  3. Given the same report asked for again, then 200 with its state and no second render.
  4. Given a worker that dies mid-report, then another worker renders it; nothing is lost.
  5. Given a passing failure, then a retry renders it; a lasting one ends FAILED with the reason, its message in the dead-letter queue.
  6. Given a slow report, then the reports after it go to the other worker.

Requirements

  • Durable queues and persistent messages.
  • Acknowledge after the work, not before.
  • Every message ends rendered, or parked with a reason: never silently gone, never retried for ever.

Learning objectives

  • Declare exchanges, queues, bindings and a dead-letter exchange.
  • Choose acknowledgement mode and prefetch, and explain Spring's "auto" against RabbitMQ's autoAck.
  • Use publisher confirms, listener retry and a message recoverer.
  • Make a consumer idempotent, and test crashes against a real broker.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Auto-ack, so messages are lost when a worker crashes.

  • Auto-ack. With the plain RabbitMQ client: a worker consumes with autoAck=true, takes the message, and its channel closes before it renders. The queue is empty. The report will never be made, and nothing records that.
  • Acknowledge after the work. The same death with autoAck=false: the message is back in the queue, and the next worker sees it marked redelivered.
  • The app. Spring's acknowledge-mode: auto acknowledges after the listener returns. In aWorkerCutOffMidRenderLosesNothing the broker closes the app's connection in the middle of a 500-page report: the report is still rendered, once.

While building, each part was undone once: acknowledge-mode: none turned 2 tests red; no retry 2; prefetch 250 1; no dead-letter exchange 1; no recoverer 1; no skip of rendered reports 1; no "requested" marker 1; no wait for the broker's confirmation 1; the marker kept after a refused publish 2. Two parts turned nothing red and stay, with their reasons: writing the PDF next to its name and moving it (so nobody reads half a PDF, which no test catches), and the worker stopping when its channel closes (see Tests).

package com.mediqo.reports;

import com.rabbitmq.client.Channel;
import com.rabbitmq.client.Connection;
import com.rabbitmq.client.ConnectionFactory;
import com.rabbitmq.client.GetResponse;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;

/**
 * A worker takes a render request and its server restarts before the PDF is made. Written first, with the plain
 * RabbitMQ client so nothing hides what the broker does.
 */
class AutoAckTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    Connection connect() throws Exception {
        ConnectionFactory factory = new ConnectionFactory();
        factory.setHost(rabbit.getHost());
        factory.setPort(rabbit.getAmqpPort());
        return factory.newConnection();
    }

    /** One worker takes the message, then dies (its channel closes) without rendering. What is left in the queue? */
    long leftAfterAWorkerDies(String queue, boolean autoAck) throws Exception {
        try (Connection connection = connect()) {
            Channel setup = connection.createChannel();
            setup.queueDeclare(queue, false, false, false, null);
            setup.basicPublish("", queue, null, "{\"reportId\":\"LR-0007\"}".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            Channel worker = connection.createChannel();
            List<String> taken = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
            worker.basicConsume(queue, autoAck, (tag, delivery) -> taken.add(new String(delivery.getBody(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)), tag -> {
            });
            await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).until(() -> taken.size() == 1);
            worker.close();   // the server restarts: no render, no acknowledgement
            await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).until(() -> setup.messageCount(queue) == (autoAck ? 0 : 1));
            if (!autoAck) {
                GetResponse again = setup.basicGet(queue, true);
                assertThat(again.getEnvelope().isRedeliver()).isTrue();   // the next worker is told it may be a repeat
            }
            long left = autoAck ? setup.messageCount(queue) : 1;
            setup.queueDelete(queue);
            return left;
        }
    }

    @Test
    void withAutoAckTheMessageIsGoneWithTheWorker() throws Exception {
        assertThat(leftAfterAWorkerDies("trap.auto-ack", true)).isZero();   // the report is never rendered, and nothing says so
    }

    @Test
    void withAcknowledgementsAfterTheWorkTheBrokerGivesItToTheNextWorker() throws Exception {
        assertThat(leftAfterAWorkerDies("trap.manual-ack", false)).isEqualTo(1);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/mediqo/reports/ReportController.java

Does
The API.
Why
Checks the id, marks the report requested (once), publishes and waits for the broker's confirmation; reads state from the report files.
Without it
A 202 for a message the broker never got; two messages for one report.
  • A refused confirmation arrives as the RabbitMQ client's ShutdownSignalException, not Spring's AmqpException: both are caught. Found while building.
  • If publishing fails, the marker is removed so the next request tries again.
package com.mediqo.reports;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonInclude;
import com.rabbitmq.client.ShutdownSignalException;
import org.springframework.amqp.AmqpException;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.core.RabbitTemplate;
import org.springframework.core.io.FileSystemResource;
import org.springframework.core.io.Resource;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.net.URI;

@RestController
class ReportController {

    @JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL)
    record ReportState(String reportId, LabReports.Status status, String pdfUrl, String failure) {
    }

    private final LabReports reports;
    private final RabbitTemplate rabbit;

    ReportController(LabReports reports, RabbitTemplate rabbit) {
        this.reports = reports;
        this.rabbit = rabbit;
    }

    /**
     * 202 once the broker has confirmed the message; the render happens on a worker. Asking again for a report that is
     * queued, ready or failed sends nothing new and answers 200 with its state.
     */
    @PostMapping("/lab-reports/{id}/render")
    ResponseEntity<ReportState> render(@PathVariable String id) throws IOException {
        known(id);
        if (!reports.markRequested(id)) {
            return ResponseEntity.ok(state(id));
        }
        try {
            rabbit.invoke(ops -> {
                ops.convertAndSend(ReportsApplication.EXCHANGE, ReportsApplication.ROUTING_KEY, new RenderWorker.RenderRequest(id));
                ops.waitForConfirmsOrDie(5_000);   // throws if the broker does not confirm in 5 s
                return null;
            });
        } catch (AmqpException | ShutdownSignalException brokerDown) {   // a refused confirm arrives as the client's own exception
            reports.unmarkRequested(id);   // nothing was queued: a later request may try again
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                    ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "The render queue is not reachable. Try again shortly."), brokerDown);
        }
        return ResponseEntity.accepted().location(URI.create("/lab-reports/" + id)).body(state(id));
    }

    @GetMapping("/lab-reports/{id}")
    ReportState report(@PathVariable String id) throws IOException {
        known(id);
        if (reports.status(id).isEmpty()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "This report has not been requested.");
        }
        return state(id);
    }

    @GetMapping("/lab-reports/{id}/pdf")
    ResponseEntity<Resource> pdf(@PathVariable String id) {
        known(id);
        if (reports.status(id).orElse(null) != LabReports.Status.READY) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No PDF for this report yet.");
        }
        return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PDF).body(new FileSystemResource(reports.pdf(id)));
    }

    private void known(String id) {
        if (!LabReports.ID.matcher(id).matches()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "A report id looks like LR-0042.");
        }
        reports.pages(id).orElseThrow(() -> problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No such report."));
    }

    private ReportState state(String id) throws IOException {
        LabReports.Status status = reports.status(id).orElseThrow();
        return new ReportState(id, status, status == LabReports.Status.READY ? "/lab-reports/" + id + "/pdf" : null, reports.failure(id).orElse(null));
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String detail) {
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail), null);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/mediqo/reports/ReportsApplication.java

Does
The topology.
Why
A direct exchange, the durable work queue with its dead-letter exchange, and the dead-letter queue; JSON messages.
Without it
Messages lost with a restart of the broker, or dropped when rejected.
package com.mediqo.reports;

import org.springframework.amqp.core.Binding;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.BindingBuilder;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.Declarables;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.DirectExchange;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.Queue;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.QueueBuilder;
import org.springframework.amqp.support.converter.JacksonJsonMessageConverter;
import org.springframework.amqp.support.converter.MessageConverter;
import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;

@SpringBootApplication
public class ReportsApplication {

    static final String EXCHANGE = "lab-reports";
    static final String QUEUE = "report-render";
    static final String DEAD_LETTERS = "lab-reports.dlx";
    static final String DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = "report-render.dlq";
    static final String ROUTING_KEY = "render";

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(ReportsApplication.class, args);
    }

    /**
     * Declared on start-up if missing: a direct exchange routes "render" to the durable work queue; a message the
     * worker gives up on goes to the dead-letter exchange and waits in its own queue for a person.
     */
    @Bean
    Declarables topology() {
        DirectExchange exchange = new DirectExchange(EXCHANGE);
        DirectExchange deadLetters = new DirectExchange(DEAD_LETTERS);
        Queue work = QueueBuilder.durable(QUEUE).deadLetterExchange(DEAD_LETTERS).deadLetterRoutingKey(ROUTING_KEY).build();
        Queue parked = QueueBuilder.durable(DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE).build();
        Binding route = BindingBuilder.bind(work).to(exchange).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        Binding parkedRoute = BindingBuilder.bind(parked).to(deadLetters).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        return new Declarables(exchange, deadLetters, work, parked, route, parkedRoute);
    }

    /** Messages as JSON, readable in the management UI. */
    @Bean
    MessageConverter json() {
        return new JacksonJsonMessageConverter();
    }
}

src/main/java/com/mediqo/reports/RenderWorker.java

Does
The worker.
Why
Skips reports already rendered, renders page by page, saves the PDF; returns normally only when done.
Without it
Lost or doubled reports when workers die or messages repeat.
  • If its channel is closed mid-render, the broker has already given the message to another worker: it stops instead of racing it.
  • The two simulated failures: LR-0013 always, LR-0042 once.
package com.mediqo.reports;

import com.rabbitmq.client.Channel;
import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.annotation.RabbitListener;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

/**
 * Takes render requests off the queue. The message is acknowledged only when this method returns: if the worker dies
 * half way, the broker gives the message to another worker. So a message can arrive twice, and a report that is
 * already rendered is skipped.
 */
@Component
class RenderWorker {

    record RenderRequest(String reportId) {
    }

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(RenderWorker.class);
    private final LabReports reports;
    private final long msPerPage;
    private final Map<String, AtomicInteger> rendered = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();   // for the tests and the logs
    private final Set<String> busyOnce = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();

    RenderWorker(LabReports reports, @Value("${mediqo.reports.ms-per-page}") long msPerPage) {
        this.reports = reports;
        this.msPerPage = msPerPage;
    }

    @RabbitListener(queues = ReportsApplication.QUEUE)
    void render(RenderRequest request, Channel channel) throws IOException, InterruptedException {
        String id = request.reportId();
        int pages = reports.pages(id).orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown report " + id));
        if (Files.exists(reports.pdf(id))) {
            log.info("{} is already rendered: a repeated message, acknowledged and skipped", id);
            return;
        }
        // Simulated lab troubles: LR-0013's scan is damaged (fails every time); LR-0042's lab system is busy once.
        if (id.equals("LR-0013")) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The scan of LR-0013 is damaged.");
        }
        if (id.equals("LR-0042") && busyOnce.add(id)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The lab system did not answer.");
        }
        List<String> lines = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int page = 1; page <= pages; page++) {
            if (!channel.isOpen()) {
                // Cut off from the broker: it has already put the message back for another worker. Stop, do not race it.
                log.warn("Lost the broker while rendering {}; another worker will take it", id);
                return;
            }
            Thread.sleep(msPerPage);   // simulated: laying out one page
            lines.add("Lab report " + id + " - page " + page + " of " + pages);
        }
        reports.savePdf(id, Pdf.of(lines));
        rendered.computeIfAbsent(id, k -> new AtomicInteger()).incrementAndGet();
    }

    int timesRendered(String id) {
        AtomicInteger n = rendered.get(id);
        return n == null ? 0 : n.get();
    }
}

Why
Writes the reason on the report, then rejects without requeue: the broker dead-letters it.
Without it
A report that fails silently, or a message retried for ever.
package com.mediqo.reports;

import org.springframework.amqp.core.Message;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.retry.MessageRecoverer;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.retry.RejectAndDontRequeueRecoverer;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;

/**
 * After the last retry: record why on the report, then reject the message without requeueing, so the broker moves
 * it to the dead-letter queue. It stays there for a person to look at or send back.
 */
@Component
class GiveUp implements MessageRecoverer {

    private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();
    private final LabReports reports;
    private final MessageRecoverer reject = new RejectAndDontRequeueRecoverer();

    GiveUp(LabReports reports) {
        this.reports = reports;
    }

    @Override
    public void recover(Message message, Throwable cause) {
        String id = JSON.readTree(message.getBody()).path("reportId").asString();
        if (reports.pages(id).isPresent()) {
            try {
                reports.saveFailure(id, rootMessage(cause));
            } catch (IOException e) {
                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
            }
        }
        reject.recover(message, cause);
    }

    private static String rootMessage(Throwable t) {
        while (t.getCause() != null) {
            t = t.getCause();
        }
        return t.getMessage();
    }
}

package com.mediqo.reports;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * The reports on disk, standing in for object storage: a marker when a render is requested, the PDF when it is done,
 * a note when it failed for good. Files survive a restart, unlike memory. Simulated lab: report LR-n has n pages
 * (LR-0001 to LR-0500).
 * shortcut: one directory on one machine; use object storage (and a table for the state) with several servers.
 */
@Component
class LabReports {

    enum Status { QUEUED, READY, FAILED }

    static final Pattern ID = Pattern.compile("LR-(\\d{4})");
    private final Path dir;

    LabReports(@Value("${mediqo.reports.dir}") Path dir) throws IOException {
        this.dir = Files.createDirectories(dir);
    }

    /** Pages of a known report; empty for one the lab does not have. */
    Optional<Integer> pages(String id) {
        Matcher m = ID.matcher(id);
        if (!m.matches()) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        int n = Integer.parseInt(m.group(1));
        return n >= 1 && n <= 500 ? Optional.of(n) : Optional.empty();
    }

    /** True the first time for a report: only then is a message sent. Atomic across threads and processes. */
    boolean markRequested(String id) {
        try {
            Files.createFile(file(id, "requested"));
            return true;
        } catch (FileAlreadyExistsException already) {
            return false;
        } catch (IOException e) {
            throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
        }
    }

    void unmarkRequested(String id) throws IOException {
        Files.deleteIfExists(file(id, "requested"));
    }

    Optional<Status> status(String id) {
        if (Files.exists(pdf(id))) {
            return Optional.of(Status.READY);
        }
        if (Files.exists(file(id, "failed"))) {
            return Optional.of(Status.FAILED);
        }
        return Files.exists(file(id, "requested")) ? Optional.of(Status.QUEUED) : Optional.empty();
    }

    Optional<String> failure(String id) throws IOException {
        Path failed = file(id, "failed");
        return Files.exists(failed) ? Optional.of(Files.readString(failed)) : Optional.empty();
    }

    /** Written next to its final name, then moved: a reader never sees half a PDF. */
    void savePdf(String id, byte[] pdf) throws IOException {
        Path tmp = Files.write(file(id, "pdf.tmp"), pdf);
        Files.move(tmp, pdf(id), StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
    }

    void saveFailure(String id, String reason) throws IOException {
        Files.writeString(file(id, "failed"), reason, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }

    Path pdf(String id) {
        return file(id, "pdf");
    }

    private Path file(String id, String kind) {
        return dir.resolve(id + "." + kind);   // id is checked against ID before any file is touched
    }
}

package com.mediqo.reports;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

final class Pdf {

    private Pdf() {
    }

    /** A minimal, valid PDF: one line of Helvetica per page. */
    static byte[] of(List<String> lines) {
        ByteArrayOutputStream out = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        List<Integer> offsets = new ArrayList<>();
        int pages = lines.size();
        int font = 3 + 2 * pages;
        StringBuilder kids = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < pages; i++) {
            kids.append(3 + 2 * i).append(" 0 R ");
        }
        write(out, "%PDF-1.4\n");
        object(out, offsets, 1, "<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>");
        object(out, offsets, 2, "<< /Type /Pages /Kids [" + kids.toString().strip() + "] /Count " + pages + " >>");
        for (int i = 0; i < pages; i++) {
            String text = "BT /F1 12 Tf 72 770 Td (" + lines.get(i) + ") Tj ET";
            object(out, offsets, 3 + 2 * i, "<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 595 842] /Contents " + (4 + 2 * i)
                    + " 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 " + font + " 0 R >> >> >>");
            object(out, offsets, 4 + 2 * i, "<< /Length " + text.length() + " >>\nstream\n" + text + "\nendstream");
        }
        object(out, offsets, font, "<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>");
        int xref = out.size();
        StringBuilder table = new StringBuilder("xref\n0 " + (offsets.size() + 1) + "\n0000000000 65535 f \n");
        offsets.forEach(o -> table.append(String.format(java.util.Locale.ROOT, "%010d 00000 n \n", o)));
        write(out, table + "trailer\n<< /Size " + (offsets.size() + 1) + " /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n" + xref + "\n%%EOF\n");
        return out.toByteArray();
    }

    private static void object(ByteArrayOutputStream out, List<Integer> offsets, int number, String body) {
        offsets.add(out.size());
        write(out, number + " 0 obj\n" + body + "\nendobj\n");
    }

    private static void write(ByteArrayOutputStream out, String s) {
        out.writeBytes(s.getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII));
    }
}

package com.mediqo.reports;

import com.rabbitmq.client.Channel;
import com.rabbitmq.client.Connection;
import com.rabbitmq.client.ConnectionFactory;
import com.rabbitmq.client.GetResponse;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;

/**
 * A worker takes a render request and its server restarts before the PDF is made. Written first, with the plain
 * RabbitMQ client so nothing hides what the broker does.
 */
class AutoAckTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    Connection connect() throws Exception {
        ConnectionFactory factory = new ConnectionFactory();
        factory.setHost(rabbit.getHost());
        factory.setPort(rabbit.getAmqpPort());
        return factory.newConnection();
    }

    /** One worker takes the message, then dies (its channel closes) without rendering. What is left in the queue? */
    long leftAfterAWorkerDies(String queue, boolean autoAck) throws Exception {
        try (Connection connection = connect()) {
            Channel setup = connection.createChannel();
            setup.queueDeclare(queue, false, false, false, null);
            setup.basicPublish("", queue, null, "{\"reportId\":\"LR-0007\"}".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            Channel worker = connection.createChannel();
            List<String> taken = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
            worker.basicConsume(queue, autoAck, (tag, delivery) -> taken.add(new String(delivery.getBody(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)), tag -> {
            });
            await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).until(() -> taken.size() == 1);
            worker.close();   // the server restarts: no render, no acknowledgement
            await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).until(() -> setup.messageCount(queue) == (autoAck ? 0 : 1));
            if (!autoAck) {
                GetResponse again = setup.basicGet(queue, true);
                assertThat(again.getEnvelope().isRedeliver()).isTrue();   // the next worker is told it may be a repeat
            }
            long left = autoAck ? setup.messageCount(queue) : 1;
            setup.queueDelete(queue);
            return left;
        }
    }

    @Test
    void withAutoAckTheMessageIsGoneWithTheWorker() throws Exception {
        assertThat(leftAfterAWorkerDies("trap.auto-ack", true)).isZero();   // the report is never rendered, and nothing says so
    }

    @Test
    void withAcknowledgementsAfterTheWorkTheBrokerGivesItToTheNextWorker() throws Exception {
        assertThat(leftAfterAWorkerDies("trap.manual-ack", false)).isEqualTo(1);
    }
}

class RetryAndDeadLetterMessagingTest extends ApiTest {

    @Autowired
    RabbitTemplate template;

    @Test
    void aBusyLabSystemIsRetriedAndTheReportIsRendered() throws Exception {
        render("LR-0042").andExpect(status().isAccepted());   // the lab system does not answer the first time
        awaitStatus("LR-0042", "READY");
        assertThat(worker.timesRendered("LR-0042")).isEqualTo(1);
        assertThat(waiting(ReportsApplication.DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE)).isZero();
    }

    @Test
    void aDamagedReportEndsInTheDeadLetterQueueWithItsReason() throws Exception {
        render("LR-0013").andExpect(status().isAccepted());
        var failed = awaitStatus("LR-0013", "FAILED");
        assertThat(failed.path("failure").asString()).isEqualTo("The scan of LR-0013 is damaged.");
        await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(5)).until(() -> waiting(ReportsApplication.DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE) == 1);
        Message parked = template.receive(ReportsApplication.DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE, 1_000);
        assertThat(new String(parked.getBody(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).isEqualTo("{\"reportId\":\"LR-0013\"}");
        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
        Map<String, Object> death = ((List<Map<String, Object>>) parked.getMessageProperties().getHeaders().get("x-death")).getFirst();
        assertThat(death).containsEntry("reason", "rejected").containsEntry("queue", ReportsApplication.QUEUE);
        assertThat(waiting(ReportsApplication.QUEUE)).isZero();   // not retried for ever
    }

    /** The broker's own view of a worker dying: its connection closed from the broker's side, mid-render. */
    @Test
    void aWorkerCutOffMidRenderLosesNothing() throws Exception {
        // The management API lists connections a few seconds late: find the app's before the render starts.
        JsonNode connections = await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(15)).until(() -> management("GET", "/api/connections"), list -> !list.isEmpty());
        render("LR-0500").andExpect(status().isAccepted());   // 500 pages: 2.5 s here
        // A worker has it and is not done: nothing waiting in the queue, and no PDF yet. (Prefetch 1: it holds just this one.)
        await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(2)).until(() -> waiting(ReportsApplication.QUEUE) == 0);
        assertThat(report("LR-0500").path("status").asString()).isEqualTo("QUEUED");
        for (JsonNode connection : connections) {
            management("DELETE", "/api/connections/" + URLEncoder.encode(connection.path("name").asString(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8).replace("+", "%20"));
        }
        awaitStatus("LR-0500", "READY");
        await().atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10)).until(() -> waiting(ReportsApplication.QUEUE) == 0);
        assertThat(worker.timesRendered("LR-0500")).isEqualTo(1);   // the cut-off worker stopped; the next one rendered it
    }

    JsonNode management(String method, String path) throws Exception {
        HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(rabbit.getHttpUrl() + path))
                .header("Authorization", "Basic " + Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString("guest:guest".getBytes()))
                .method(method, HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.noBody()).build();
        try (HttpClient http = HttpClient.newHttpClient()) {
            String body = http.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString()).body();
            return body.isBlank() ? JSON.createObjectNode() : JSON.readTree(body);
        }
    }
}

    ResponseEntity<ReportState> render(@PathVariable String id, @RequestParam(defaultValue = "false") boolean urgent) throws IOException {

                ops.convertAndSend(ReportsApplication.EXCHANGE, ReportsApplication.ROUTING_KEY, new RenderWorker.RenderRequest(id), message -> {

            reports.unmarkRequested(id);   // nothing was queued: a later request may try again
            throw new ErrorResponseException(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                    ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, "The render queue is not reachable. Try again shortly."), brokerDown);

     * before it is acknowledged on the dead-letter queue, so a crash in between duplicates it rather than losing it.
     * shortcut: no sign-in in this station; an endpoint like this is for operators only.

            GetResponse parked = channel.basicGet(ReportsApplication.DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE, false);
            if (parked == null) {
                return false;
            }
            String id = tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper.builder().build().readTree(parked.getBody()).path("reportId").asString();
            if (reports.pages(id).isPresent()) {
                reports.clearFailure(id);
            }
            channel.basicPublish(ReportsApplication.EXCHANGE, ReportsApplication.ROUTING_KEY, parked.getProps(), parked.getBody());
            channel.basicAck(parked.getEnvelope().getDeliveryTag(), false);
            return true;
        }))) {
            moved++;
        }
        return new Replayed(moved);

package com.mediqo.reports;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.FileAlreadyExistsException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * The reports on disk, standing in for object storage: a marker when a render is requested, the PDF when it is done,
 * a note when it failed for good. Files survive a restart, unlike memory. Simulated lab: report LR-n has n pages
 * (LR-0001 to LR-0500).
 * shortcut: one directory on one machine; use object storage (and a table for the state) with several servers.
 */
@Component
class LabReports {

    enum Status { QUEUED, READY, FAILED }

    static final Pattern ID = Pattern.compile("LR-(\\d{4})");
    private final Path dir;

    LabReports(@Value("${mediqo.reports.dir}") Path dir) throws IOException {
        this.dir = Files.createDirectories(dir);
    }

    /** Pages of a known report; empty for one the lab does not have. */
    Optional<Integer> pages(String id) {
        Matcher m = ID.matcher(id);
        if (!m.matches()) {
            return Optional.empty();
        }
        int n = Integer.parseInt(m.group(1));
        return n >= 1 && n <= 500 ? Optional.of(n) : Optional.empty();
    }

    /** True the first time for a report: only then is a message sent. Atomic across threads and processes. */
    boolean markRequested(String id) {
        try {
            Files.createFile(file(id, "requested"));
            return true;
        } catch (FileAlreadyExistsException already) {
            return false;
        } catch (IOException e) {
            throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
        }
    }

    void unmarkRequested(String id) throws IOException {
        Files.deleteIfExists(file(id, "requested"));
    }

    Optional<Status> status(String id) {
        if (Files.exists(pdf(id))) {
            return Optional.of(Status.READY);
        }
        if (Files.exists(file(id, "failed"))) {
            return Optional.of(Status.FAILED);
        }
        return Files.exists(file(id, "requested")) ? Optional.of(Status.QUEUED) : Optional.empty();
    }

    Optional<String> failure(String id) throws IOException {
        Path failed = file(id, "failed");
        return Files.exists(failed) ? Optional.of(Files.readString(failed)) : Optional.empty();
    }

    /** Written next to its final name, then moved: a reader never sees half a PDF. */
    void savePdf(String id, byte[] pdf) throws IOException {
        Path tmp = Files.write(file(id, "pdf.tmp"), pdf);
        Files.move(tmp, pdf(id), StandardCopyOption.ATOMIC_MOVE, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
    }

    void saveFailure(String id, String reason) throws IOException {
        Files.writeString(file(id, "failed"), reason, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }

    /** Challenge 1: a report sent back to the queue is no longer failed. */
    void clearFailure(String id) throws IOException {
        Files.deleteIfExists(file(id, "failed"));
    }

    Path pdf(String id) {
        return file(id, "pdf");
    }

    private Path file(String id, String kind) {
        return dir.resolve(id + "." + kind);   // id is checked against ID before any file is touched
    }
}

    static final String QUEUE = "report-render";
    static final String DEAD_LETTERS = "lab-reports.dlx";
    static final String DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = "report-render.dlq";
    static final String ROUTING_KEY = "render";

        SpringApplication.run(ReportsApplication.class, args);
    }

    /**
     * Declared on start-up if missing: a direct exchange routes "render" to the durable work queue; a message the
     * worker gives up on goes to the dead-letter exchange and waits in its own queue for a person.
     */
    @Bean
    Declarables topology() {
        DirectExchange exchange = new DirectExchange(EXCHANGE);
        DirectExchange deadLetters = new DirectExchange(DEAD_LETTERS);
        // Challenge 2: a priority queue (0 to 10). Queue arguments cannot change on an existing queue: a new queue, or a migration.
        Queue work = QueueBuilder.durable(QUEUE).deadLetterExchange(DEAD_LETTERS).deadLetterRoutingKey(ROUTING_KEY).maxPriority(10).build();
        Queue parked = QueueBuilder.durable(DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE).build();
        Binding route = BindingBuilder.bind(work).to(exchange).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        Binding parkedRoute = BindingBuilder.bind(parked).to(deadLetters).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        return new Declarables(exchange, deadLetters, work, parked, route, parkedRoute);
    }

    /** Messages as JSON, readable in the management UI. */
    @Bean
    MessageConverter json() {
        return new JacksonJsonMessageConverter();
    }
}

RabbitMQ or Kafka?

Mediqo also wants every lab result as an event that billing, the patient app and analytics read on their own, and can read again from last month. Which part stays a RabbitMQ work queue and which becomes a Kafka topic? Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test with the plain client: auto-ack against manual ack.
  2. Declare the topology: exchange, durable queue, dead-letter exchange and queue.
  3. Publish with confirms; consume with acknowledgement after the work, prefetch 1.
  4. Add retry, the recoverer and idempotency; then cut a worker off in a test.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Acknowledge after the work, retry, dead-letter queueRepeats are possible: the worker must skip them.Chosen
Auto-ack (acknowledge-mode: none)A worker that dies loses its messages.The trap
Requeue on every failureA message that always fails loops for ever.Avoid
@Async in the app (station 098's way)No broker; jobs die with the server.For work you can lose
KafkaA log that consumers read at their own pace and can replay; work-queue semantics need share groups or care.For events, see challenge 3

Database design

No database: the broker holds the work, the disk holds the reports. With several servers, report state moves to a table and files to object storage; the queue stays the same.

A Working Systems station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Quorum queues
On a RabbitMQ cluster, use quorum queues for work that must survive a node: classic queues live on one node.
Watch
Queue depth, unacknowledged messages, consumer count and the dead-letter queue's size. A growing dead-letter queue is a bug report.
Timeouts
RabbitMQ closes a channel whose delivery is not acknowledged within consumer_timeout (30 minutes by default): long tasks must fit, or be split.
Poison messages
The retry limit is what keeps one bad message from blocking a worker for ever.

Interview takeaways

Why do messages get lost with auto-ack?

The broker deletes a message as soon as it is sent to a consumer. If the consumer dies before finishing, nobody has it.

What does Spring AMQP's acknowledge-mode auto mean?

Spring acknowledges after the listener returns normally and rejects on an exception: the safe default. RabbitMQ's autoAck is Spring's NONE.

What is prefetch for?

How many unacknowledged messages a consumer may hold. 1 spreads long tasks fairly; higher is faster for tiny ones.

How do you stop a poison message looping?

Retry a few times, then reject without requeue so the broker dead-letters it.

How does the API know the broker has the message?

Publisher confirms: wait for the broker's ack before answering 202.

Why must consumers be idempotent?

Delivery is at least once: a crash after the work and before the ack means the message comes again.

package com.mediqo.reports;

import org.springframework.amqp.core.AcknowledgeMode;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.Binding;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.BindingBuilder;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.Declarables;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.DirectExchange;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.Queue;
import org.springframework.amqp.core.QueueBuilder;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.config.SimpleRabbitListenerContainerFactory;
import org.springframework.amqp.rabbit.connection.ConnectionFactory;
import org.springframework.amqp.support.converter.JacksonJsonMessageConverter;
import org.springframework.amqp.support.converter.MessageConverter;
import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;

@SpringBootApplication
public class ReportsApplication {

    static final String EXCHANGE = "lab-reports";
    static final String QUEUE = "report-render";
    static final String DEAD_LETTERS = "lab-reports.dlx";
    static final String DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE = "report-render.dlq";
    static final String ROUTING_KEY = "render";

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(ReportsApplication.class, args);
    }

    /**
     * Declared on start-up if missing: a direct exchange routes "render" to the durable work queue; a message the
     * worker gives up on goes to the dead-letter exchange and waits in its own queue for a person.
     */
    @Bean
    Declarables topology() {
        DirectExchange exchange = new DirectExchange(EXCHANGE);
        DirectExchange deadLetters = new DirectExchange(DEAD_LETTERS);
        Queue work = QueueBuilder.durable(QUEUE).deadLetterExchange(DEAD_LETTERS).deadLetterRoutingKey(ROUTING_KEY).build();
        Queue parked = QueueBuilder.durable(DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE).build();
        Binding route = BindingBuilder.bind(work).to(exchange).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        Binding parkedRoute = BindingBuilder.bind(parked).to(deadLetters).with(ROUTING_KEY);
        return new Declarables(exchange, deadLetters, work, parked, route, parkedRoute);
    }

    /** Auto-ack: faster, and the worker is simpler without acknowledgements. */
    @Bean
    SimpleRabbitListenerContainerFactory rabbitListenerContainerFactory(ConnectionFactory connections, MessageConverter json) {
        SimpleRabbitListenerContainerFactory factory = new SimpleRabbitListenerContainerFactory();
        factory.setConnectionFactory(connections);
        factory.setMessageConverter(json);
        factory.setAcknowledgeMode(AcknowledgeMode.NONE);
        factory.setConcurrentConsumers(2);
        return factory;
    }

    /** Messages as JSON, readable in the management UI. */
    @Bean
    MessageConverter json() {
        return new JacksonJsonMessageConverter();
    }
}

Findings

1AcknowledgeMode.NONE

"Auto-ack: faster": the broker now deletes each message the moment a worker receives it. A worker that dies mid-report loses it, and a listener that throws loses it too: there is nothing left to retry or dead-letter.

Test evidence: aWorkerCutOffMidRenderLosesNothing and aDamagedReportEndsInTheDeadLetterQueueWithItsReason fail.

2A hand-made factory drops Spring Boot's settings

Declaring rabbitListenerContainerFactory replaces the one Spring Boot builds from application.yaml: prefetch 1, the retry policy and the recoverer are all gone, with nothing in the code to say so.

Test evidence: aSlowReportDoesNotHoldUpTheOnesBehindIt and aBusyLabSystemIsRetriedAndTheReportIsRendered fail: no prefetch 1, no retry.
